item.text:
Define
\[
Z=\{x\in U:\ f \text{ vanishes on a neighborhood of }x\}.
\]
Show that \(Z\) is both relatively open and relatively closed in \(U\).

Relative openness is immediate. For closedness, let \(x\in U\) lie in the closure of \(Z\). Analyticity supplies a local Taylor expansion
\[
f(x+h)=\sum_{n\ge 0} P_n(h)
\]
by continuous homogeneous polynomials. At points of \(Z\), every Taylor coefficient (equivalently, every iterated derivative) vanishes. Continuity of these coefficients as the center varies then forces all coefficients at \(x\) to vanish, so the expansion shows that \(f\) is zero near \(x\). Thus \(x\in Z\).

The hypothesis gives \(Z\neq\varnothing\), and preconnectedness of \(U\) forces the nonempty clopen subset \(Z\) to equal \(U\). Completeness of \(F\) is essential for the convergent power-series/Taylor representation and its uniqueness.
